hints.S03_A1: The dash explains it: her arms were TOO tired to lift anything, and they are compared to NOODLES. Ask: are cooked noodles firm and springy, or floppy and drooping? Match the adjective to the noodles, not to temperature.
hints.S03_A2: Look at the tools Father is using: some wood and GLUE. Ask: what do you do to a chair that is already broken - damage it further, or repair it? The tools tell you the purpose of the action.
hints.S03_A3: The children help after dinner and also WASH the dishes. Ask: what would a helpful child do to a table covered in used plates - remove them tidily, or attack the furniture? Pick the phrasal verb that tidies, not one that harms.
hints.S03_A4: The dash gives you the meaning: she could not stop SMILING. Ask: which idiom means extremely happy? The other three describe being ill, being in trouble, or feeling sad - none of those make you smile.
hints.S03_A5: Notice she was SAVING that last piece for herself, and her brother ate it without asking. Ask: is that a welcome surprise or an unwelcome one? Choose the feeling that matches losing something you wanted.
hints.S03_B1: The subject is NOBODY. Even though it feels like many people, nobody / everybody / someone behave as a single person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the one ending in -s?
hints.S03_B2: The helper HAS is already sitting in the sentence. Ask: after have/has, which form builds the present perfect? Not the base form, not the -ing form - you need the third form of the verb.
hints.S03_B3: Mother CAME home - that is the sudden event. The brother's job was already going on when she walked in. Ask: which tense shows an action in progress that gets interrupted by something sudden?
hints.S03_B4: The word MUCH in front of the blank is a comparison signal, and only two states are compared: the house before cleaning and after. Ask: does comparing two things need the comparative or the superlative? And never stack 'more' in front of an -er ending.
hints.S03_B5: Every single child took part - the sentence says they helped to CARRY the bags upstairs. Ask: which word means the whole group acting as one, rather than one-by-one? And be careful not to pick a word that would make the sentence mean nobody helped.
hints.S03_B6: Look at the main clause: keeping a tidy home IS everyone's RESPONSIBILITY - a positive statement built on the 'to be' verb. Ask: does a positive statement take a positive tag, or its opposite? The tag must also reuse the same verb, not a different helper.
hints.S03_B7: The subject is the TWINS - two people, and they are not the speaker. Ask: does the reflexive pronoun point back to one boy, to a thing, to us, or to them? Match it to who actually did the cleaning.
hints.S03_B8: Look at the word right after the blank: WITH. It forms a fixed phrase joining Aunt Mary to the people who came along. Ask: which option normally pairs with 'with' to mean 'accompanied by'? Say each choice aloud and hear which sounds right.
hints.S03_C1: 'EVERY SATURDAY' means this happens again and again, so the verb is present - and 'my father' is one person. Ask: in the present, does a singular subject take the plain verb or the verb ending in -s?
hints.S03_C2: 'LAST SATURDAY' is finished time, so this verb must be past. Ask: which form shows a completed action - the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the one that adds -ed?
hints.S03_C3: Look at the word before the blank: 'in CHARGE OF ___'. Ask: after a preposition like 'of', which form must a verb take? Never the plain form, and never the past form.
hints.S03_C4: 'She SPENT nearly an HOUR ___' - spend time doing something. Ask: which form follows 'spent an hour'? And the corners are being wiped with a mop, not dusted, so choose the right verb too.
hints.S03_C5: After 'I HAD TO ___' the verb must be in its plainest form, with no ending at all. Ask: which of the two base verbs in the box is the one you do to a FLOOR with a bucket of water, rather than the general word for tidying?
hints.S03_C6: The SHELVES were done and the BOOKS were put back - all finished, in the past. Ask: which past form fits a verb that simply adds -ed? Shelves are wiped, not mopped, so pick the right verb as well.
hints.S03_C7: 'EVEN NOW' means it is happening at this very moment - the action is not finished. Ask: which choice shows an action in progress right now? One brother is doing it, so the helping verb must be singular.
hints.S03_C8: 'What a ___ and TIDY home!' - the blank sits beside 'tidy', so it must be a describing word too. Ask: which choice is an adjective? An -ing form or a past form would not fit next to 'tidy'.
hints.S03_D1: He did not want to DROP the pot of water, so he took his time. Ask: does the blank describe HOW he carried it? Then it needs an -ly word - the one about taking care, not the one about speed.
hints.S03_D2: He spilt water even though he was trying hard - his hands were not steady. Ask: which box word describes a person who knocks things over and drops things? It is a describing word, after 'a little'.
hints.S03_D3: The water ended up ON THE FLOOR, so something happened to it as he carried the pot. Ask: which box word is a past verb meaning that liquid went where it should not?
hints.S03_D4: He had to finish BEFORE his MOTHER came back into the kitchen - there was no time to lose. Ask: which -ly word describes doing something fast?
hints.S03_D5: He WIPED the water up before Mother arrived, so the floor no longer looked messy. Ask: which box word describes a room that is neat and in order? It goes in front of the noun 'kitchen'.
hints.S03_E1: TAKE is an irregular verb, so -ed is wrong. Ask: how would you say it in the past - 'yesterday she ___ the bus'? Irregular verbs change their shape instead of adding an ending.
hints.S03_E2: The whole passage is about LAST SATURDAY, and the verbs around it (mopped, wiped, swept) are past. Ask: is the underlined verb past or present? Every verb in the story must share the same tense.
hints.S03_E3: Find the subject: THE CURTAINS - more than one. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular verb, or the plural one? Match the verb to the subject, not to the word next to it.
hints.S03_E4: The best work BELONGS TO the cleaners - more than one cleaner. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or only make a plural? Where does the apostrophe go when the owners are many?
hints.S03_E5: The HOME belongs to the family Grandma is talking about. Ask: does the underlined spelling mean 'at that place', or 'belonging to them'? The two sound alike, so choose by meaning.
hints.S03_F1: A past yes/no question ('DID you remember...?') becomes REPORTED speech. Ask: which joining word follows ASKED? Does 'you' stay as 'you'? And when the reporting verb is past, what happens to the verb inside - does it step one tense further back?
hints.S03_F2: One action was already going on when the other cut across it. Ask: which sentence describes the longer action in progress, and which describes the sudden one? Put WHEN in front of the sudden one.
